newsitem.title: THAILAND: FOCUS-Bangkok Land hit by property woes.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bangkok Land hit by property woes.

text.p: Major Thai property developer Bangkok Land Plc reported poor 1996/97 earnings thanks to the twin problems of pre-sales pledges without the certainty of payment and a glut in supply, analysts said on Monday.

Bangkok Land's problems were similar to other property developers in Thailand as it recorded lower payment figures in the pre-sales account, while not knowing whether buyers would be able to pay the rest of the money.
"Oversupply on housing also poses a major problem and this has led to a fierce competition among the developers," said Samart Rusmeerojwong of James Capel Asia.

Bangkok Land shares ended unchanged at 10.25 baht on Monday after the firjm announced that consolidated net profit for the year ended March 31, 1997, plunged to 7.37 million baht ($296,000) compared to 608.20 million the previous year.

Thailand's property sector has been grappling with a host of problems such as oversupply, double-digit interest rates which have further sapped lacklustre demand, and over-leveraged and inexperienced property and development firms that have begun to collapse.

Traders said Bangkok Land's reputation was not good in the eyes of the public although it had received a contract from the government to build a sports complex for the Asian Games to be held in Bangkok in December 1998.

"Several buyers have lodged complaints with the police against Bangkok Land over its failure to build infrastructure as promised earlier. Several of its new projects are also unsold at present," said Samart.
